title: The Corruption of Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The corruption of sin means that sin damages the whole person, distorting worship, desires, thinking, relationships, speech, and judgment. Sin does not remain isolated; it spreads its effects through human life.
summary: The corruption of sin means that sin damages the whole person, distorting worship, desires, thinking, relationships, speech, and judgment. Sin does not remain isolated; it spreads its effects through human life.
christFocus: Jesus Christ redeems corrupted sinners and begins restoring them into holiness, truth, love, and soundness before God. His grace reaches deeper than outward behavior.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin corrupts more than actions. It affects desires, thinking, motives, worship, relationships, and perception of truth. Fallen people do not see God, themselves, or others rightly apart from grace.

This corruption is seen in Scripture as darkened understanding, hardened hearts, foolish exchange of truth for lies, and disordered desires. Sin bends the person inward and away from God.

The corruption of sin helps explain why people can defend what harms them, desire what enslaves them, and reject the truth that would save them. Sin disorders loves and clouds judgment.

Christ renews corrupted people from the inside out. Believers put off the old self and are renewed in the spirit of their minds, learning truth as it is in Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If sin is seen only as outward bad behavior, the answer will be shallow behavior control. Scripture shows that the problem reaches deeper and that transformation must reach the heart.

This doctrine helps believers understand why growth can be slow and why they need continual renewal. Christ is not ashamed to restore deeply damaged people; His grace reaches the places sin has corrupted.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to renew the parts of you that sin has distorted. Do not only stop outward acts while protecting inward corruption. Bring desires, thoughts, relationships, and habits under Scripture, and trust Christ to restore you by His Word and Spirit.
